address-book.context: Ring-bound book with a person on its cover and tabs along the spine. Used for contact lists, phone books, directories, CRM address records and saved recipients.

announcement.context: Rectangular speech bubble with an exclamation mark inside. Used for announcements, news posts, important notices, product updates, service alerts and pinned messages.

antenna.context: Radio mast with a transmitter at its tip sending out waves on both sides. Used for radio stations, cell towers, network coverage, transmission status and broadcasting.

bell.context: Plain bell with a clapper at its base. Used for the notifications button, alert settings, reminders, subscribe prompts and inbox of updates.

broadcast.context: Central dot with curved signal waves on both sides. Used for live status, going on air, radio and wireless signals, broadcast messages to many users and hotspots.

chat.context: Rectangular speech bubble with a pointed tail at the bottom left. Used for chat buttons, comments, messaging apps, live support widgets and reply actions.

chat-bubbles.context: Two round speech bubbles overlapping, one large and one small, with tails on opposite sides. Used for conversations, group chat, discussion forums, messaging tabs and community Q&A.

chat-dots.context: Rectangular speech bubble holding three dots. Used for chat buttons, unread messages, SMS threads, comments and a message waiting to be read or written.

chat-typing.context: Pill-shaped bubble with three dots and a trail of two small circles. Used as the typing indicator in chats, a pending reply, a bot thinking and live-chat status.

comment-dots.context: Round speech bubble with three dots in the middle. Used for comments, replies, discussion threads, add-a-comment buttons and someone composing a reply.

contact.context: Head and shoulders of a person with a telephone handset beside them. Used for contact us pages, calling a contact, customer service numbers and phone details in profiles.

conversation.context: Two rectangular speech bubbles coming from opposite sides, one above the other. Used for dialogue, back-and-forth replies, interviews, chat history and discussions.

email-at.context: Envelope with a large @ sign at its corner. Used for email address fields, contact details, email sign-up, verification messages and mailing settings.

fax.context: Fax machine with a keypad and a sheet of paper rising from the top. Used for fax numbers on contact pages, office equipment, sending documents and old-style business details.

headset-support.context: Head wearing an over-ear headset with a microphone arm. Used for customer support, help desks, call centres, live agents and contact support buttons.

inbox-full.context: Inbox tray with a stack of papers resting in it. Used for unread messages, a full inbox, pending tasks, received files and an in-tray of documents.

intercom.context: Wall-mounted panel with a round speaker grille and a call button. Used for building entry systems, door phones, apartment buzzers, reception calls and smart home access.

letter.context: Closed envelope sealed with a round wax seal where the flap meets. Used for letters, invitations, formal messages, postal mail and private or sealed correspondence.

mail.context: Closed envelope with its flap folded down in a V. Used for email buttons, the inbox, contact links, newsletters and anywhere a message can be sent or read.

mail-flag.context: Closed envelope with a small flag on a pole at its right. Used for flagged emails, messages marked for follow-up, important mail and priority filters in an inbox.

mail-open.context: Opened envelope with its flap raised. Used for read emails, mark as read, opened messages, invitations and inbox states once a message has been viewed.

mail-stack.context: Two envelopes, one stacked behind the other. Used for multiple emails, bulk mail, mail merges, email campaigns, message folders and all-mail views.

mailbox.context: Curbside mailbox on a post with its flag raised. Used for postal mail, delivery addresses, new mail notices, parcel drop-offs and home or shipping settings.

megaphone.context: Hand-held megaphone with a trigger handle, pointing up to the right. Used for marketing campaigns, announcements, promotions, public notices and shout-outs.

message-circle.context: Round speech bubble with a small pointed tail at the lower left. Used for messages, chat buttons, comments, replies and messaging tabs in mobile apps.

message-square.context: Square speech bubble whose bottom-left corner extends into the tail. Used for messages, comments, SMS, chat entries and message buttons in toolbars.

messages.context: Two overlapping rectangular speech bubbles, one behind the other. Used for message threads, inbox lists, direct messages, conversations and chat history.

newsletter.context: Page with a masthead and text lines sliding out of an open envelope. Used for newsletter sign-ups, email digests, subscriptions, bulletins and email marketing.

pager.context: Small pager with a text display and a button below it. Used for on-call alerts, hospital staff paging, restaurant table buzzers and incident notifications.

paper-plane.context: Folded paper plane flying up and to the right. Used for send buttons, sharing, direct messages, delivered status and email or chat submit actions.

phone.context: Classic telephone handset tilted on its side. Used for call buttons, phone numbers, contact details, dialers, support lines and click-to-call links.

phone-call.context: Telephone handset with two sound arcs above it. Used for an active call, calling now, voice call buttons, ringing status and call in progress screens.

phone-incoming.context: Telephone handset with an arrow pointing in toward it. Used for incoming calls, received calls in call logs, inbound lines and answer call prompts.

phone-missed.context: Telephone handset with an arrow that bends back on itself. Used for missed calls in call logs, unanswered call alerts, callback reminders and notifications.

phone-outgoing.context: Telephone handset with an arrow pointing away up to the right. Used for outgoing calls, dialled numbers in call logs, place a call and outbound call reports.

phone-ringing.context: Telephone handset with short ringing marks beside it. Used for a ringing phone, incoming call alerts, ringtone settings, vibrate mode and wake-up calls.

podcast.context: Studio microphone with curved sound waves on both sides. Used for podcast players, episode lists, audio shows, recording studios and listen buttons.

postcard.context: Postcard with a stamp in the top corner, a message area and address lines. Used for travel greetings, holiday mail, direct mail campaigns, gift cards and postal services.

quote-bubble.context: Speech bubble holding a pair of quotation marks. Used for testimonials, customer quotes, cited replies, quote posts and review snippets.

rss.context: Dot in the corner with two quarter-circle arcs spreading out from it. Used for RSS and Atom feeds, blog subscriptions, news readers and podcast feed links.

satellite-dish.context: Satellite dish on a stand, aimed up and to the right with a receiver arm. Used for satellite TV, signal reception, space communication, ground stations and broadcast links.

send.context: Arrowhead pointing right with a notch cut into its tail. Used for send buttons in chats and email, submit actions, forwarding a message and post comment controls.

signal-bars.context: Four bars rising in height from left to right. Used for cellular signal strength, network reception, connection quality, Wi-Fi strength and level meters.

speakerphone.context: Mobile phone with sound waves coming from its side. Used for putting a call on speaker, hands-free mode, loudspeaker settings and conference calls.

speech-bubble.context: Oval speech bubble with a curved tail at the bottom left. Used for dialogue, comic speech, quotes, voice or talk buttons and someone saying something.

stamp-postage.context: Postage stamp with perforated edges and a small picture of hills inside. Used for postage, mailing costs, postal services, stamp collecting and sending letters.

telegram-message.context: Strip of telegraph tape printed with dots and dashes of Morse code. Used for telegrams, urgent short messages, Morse code topics, history of communication and retro messaging.

thought-bubble.context: Cloud-shaped bubble with a trail of small circles leading down to it. Used for thoughts, ideas, daydreams, thinking states, brainstorming and comic inner monologue.

video-call.context: Video camera with a person shown inside its body. Used for video calls, video chat buttons, online meetings, webcam settings and telehealth appointments.

voicemail.context: Two circles joined by a straight line at their base, like the reels of a tape. Used for voicemail messages, answering machines, voice memos and missed call recordings.

walkie-talkie.context: Hand-held two-way radio with a short antenna and a speaker grille. Used for push-to-talk buttons, team radio channels, security staff, events crews and outdoor communication.
